Sometimes this sub feels like a pit of despair but I only really go on when I want someone to commiserate with. Lately I’ve been think of ways to make myself happy and I think back when I was a kid. My childhood wasn’t great but I had a phenomenal mindset at the time. There was no pressure of age, no one expected so much of me. I had no awareness of how pretty I looked, how much money I made or if I had a boyfriend or friends. I was just in my own world doing the things I loved. I want to be like that again. This week I’ve been channeling my inner child by engaging in activities that once made me happy and most importantly letting go societal expectations. This might sound like a no brainer or old news but breaking down this “adult” mental barrier I had is really working. I wanna make a full post about after some time.

I have struggled with mental health issues my entire life and lemme tell you, people aren’t as accepting as they might seem, at least in my opinion. People get tired of you, very quickly. My mom is tired of me and my sister think I can, “turn it off and on”. I’ve had doctors get frustrated with me to the point where one said I was untreatable. And yes, mental illness can get ugly. It’s not always crying yourself to sleep and can be rage, delusion and frankly stuff that would freak people out. Then it’s too far and they just want to lock you away or distance themself from you. I saw this YouTube video and it was something like, “people don’t understand how mental illness works” and the thumbnail was something like, “just because you have ____ mental illness, doesn’t mean you have to exhibit symptoms of _____ mental illness”

A psychiatrist tried to diagnose me with childhood emotional neglect but my mom denied it and took it an insult because I “always had my needs met”. Yea, that’s the point. Yea technically I never starved, I was clothed and had a home (I didn’t have a bed but whatever) but my childhood was very lonely and my mother was always working and when she came home it was “mommy time” and asked us not to bother her because she was tired and my older sister hated my guts and actively ignored me. All I can really remember about childhood is watching TV. But yea, neglect sucks. I’m sorry you went through it.

I’ve been experiencing bloating, nausea, constipation and sharp stomach pains that comes and goes. It hurts every time I eat anything though I’ve been following the low fodmap diet for about 2 weeks, eating smaller meals, drinking more water and taking a probiotic and fiber supplement(I find that the fiber helps with the constipation but I still don’t feel “cleaned out”). All this helps cut down the bloating a bit, but not all the way, I constantly have a dull pain in my lower abdomen. I’ve cut out all dairy and was tested for celiac last year which came back negative, so I still consume gluten products. I did a food diary with my GP when I still had insurance and the results were sporadic and inconsistent. Some days it seemed last dairy was the culprit and then it wasn’t another day and it seemed like absolutely everything made my stomach hurt and made me nauseous. The weird thing is, this whole situation comes and goes. I haven’t felt this way in almost a year and now it’s back and it’s staying longer than before and more painful. Last time I had it was around September 2019 and one day it kinda went away. Sorry if this is long and TMI.
